record.original_question: In the three-body problem (n=2), assuming the total energy is negative and even restricting to planar motion, can the moment of inertia grow to infinity as t→∞ for a dense open set of initial conditions? The source also asks the analogous question for n>2.

evidence.quote: Problem 3.3.1 (G.D. Birkhoff) Let n = 2 (three body problem) and as­ sume that the total eneryy is negative. One can even assume that the three particles move on a fixed plane. Is it true that the moment of inertia of the system can grow to 00 as t -t 00 for a dense open set of initial conditions? One can ask the same question for n > 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Newtonian n+1-body problem in $\mathbb{R}^d$: point masses $m_0, m_1, \dots, m_n > 0$ with positions $q_0(t), \dots, q_n(t) \in \mathbb{R}^d$ evolving according to
$$ m_i \ddot q_i = \sum_{j \neq i} \frac{m_i m_j (q_j - q_i)}{\|q_j - q_i\|^3}, \qquad i = 0, 1, \dots, n. $$
The total energy is $H = \tfrac{1}{2}\sum_i m_i \|\dot q_i\|^2 - \sum_{i<j} \frac{m_i m_j}{\|q_i - q_j\|}$, and the moment of inertia about the center of mass is
$$ I(t) = \sum_{i=0}^n m_i \|q_i(t) - q_{\mathrm{cm}}\|^2, \qquad q_{\mathrm{cm}} = \frac{\sum_i m_i q_i}{\sum_i m_i}. $$
Restrict to initial conditions with $H < 0$ (negative total energy), so that the system is bounded in mean (and one may further restrict to planar motion, $d = 2$).

(a) For $n = 2$ (the three-body problem in the plane with negative total energy), is it true that the set of initial conditions for which $I(t) \to \infty$ as $t \to \infty$ contains a dense open subset of the phase space of bounded-energy initial data?

(b) Answer the analogous question for general $n \geq 3$.
artifact.status_search_result: Birkhoff's question on whether $I(t) \to \infty$ on a dense open set of negative-energy initial conditions in the three-body problem appears still open. Recent work (e.g., on three-body orbits with large potential) revisits Birkhoff's arguments and constructs orbits with $\limsup I(t) = \infty$ in open sets of initial data, but does not establish density or settle the conjecture. No source in the search shows the conjecture has been proved or disproved.

status_evidence.title: Orbits of the three-body problem with large potential
status_evidence.snippet: Birkhoff's goal was to prove a result of Sundman... The set of initial conditions of the regularized problem leading to solutions [with large potential] has nonempty interior.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work constructs open sets of orbits with large potential, building on Birkhoff's program, but does not resolve the density question.

status_evidence.title: A brief account of G.D. Birkhoff's problem in the problem of three bodies
status_evidence.snippet: Account of G.D. Birkhoff's problem in the three-body problem.
status_evidence.claim: The Birkhoff problem on the asymptotic behavior of the moment of inertia is recognized as a standing open problem in celestial mechanics.
